newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Grain futures fall in Budapest mkt in solid trade.
newsitem.headline: Grain futures fall in Budapest mkt in solid trade.

text.p: Virtually all grain futures prices fell on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) on Wednesday in above-average trading activity, partly on fundamentals and partly on profit-taking, dealers said.
"There were speculative games on the wheat market but maize was dominated by physical-related trades," said Sandor Torok of Agrokont.

Maize and wheat fell for all maturities, with maize edging down 170 to 18,900 for March and dropping by the daily limit of 400 forints to 18,100 for July. Wheat also dropped by 400 to 28,210 for March.
Turnover was 1,302 contracts or 522.6 million forints.
Torok said that the market continued to worry that Hungary would not be able to export all its excess maize of between 500,000 and one million tonnes.

But March maize contracts might have reached support for now because the government's recent decision to give export permits for 200,000 tonnes was bound to have a beneficial effect on maize prices in the short term, said Gabor Bidlo of Agrograin.
As for wheat, players were trying to cash in on earlier gains, which were fuelled by speculation that a relatively cold January hurt the Hungarian winter wheat crop, Bidlo said.
Overall, however, the outlook was good for wheat because export stocks were low and there was plenty of Ukrainian and Serbian demand for the old crop, Torok said.
Lot size on the BCE is 20,000 kgs for all contracts.
